📋 Executive summary in-progress Infrastructure landed and the cascade is functional across TWO cell generations (real divisions at the ~700 fg threshold). Feature-off is…

Two new process-bigraph Steps plus the ParCa data + wiring that drive them:

1. ecoli-flagella-transcription-regulation — the Kalir & Alon bilinear SUM-gate. Promoter activity = weighted sum of FlhD4C2 (CPLX0-3930) and free FliA/sigma28 (EG11355-MONOMER); Class II weighted to FlhDC, Class III to FliA. Writes a per-promoter init_prob_override for 7 Class II + 9 Class III TUs (incl. flgM, closing the negative-feedback loop). transcript_initiation substitutes the override where > 0.

2. ecoli-flagella-flgm-secretion — depletes cytoplasmic FlgM (G369-MONOMER[c]) proportional to complete flagella (CPLX0-7452[j]); the Class II -> Class III timing gate that releases sequestered FliA after basal-body completion.

Supporting data: FLGM-FLIA-CPLX sequestration equilibrium, an init_prob_override field on the promoter unique molecule, and a metabolism guard so a protein-protein equilibrium coexists with ParCa biomass fitting.

in-progress Current verdict. Infrastructure landed and the cascade is functional across TWO cell generations (real divisions at the ~700 fg threshold). Feature-off is seam-neutral; with the cascade on, the SUM-gate holds Class II > Class III and FlgM secretion releases bounded free FliA.

COUNT VERDICT (settled) — the cascade does NOT reduce flagellar overexpression; under proper calibration it INCREASES it. The fast-mode cache suggested a reduction (OFF g1=53,g2=44 vs ON g1=44,g2=34), but a 4-seed x 3-gen ensemble on the FULL-mode (calibrated) cache robustly reverses that: ON means 62.5/54.8/59.0 vs OFF means 49.5/44.2/40.8 (ON > OFF in 11 of 12 seed-generations). So the reduction was a fast-mode artifact; Maya's overexpression-reduction hypothesis is REFUTED for the cascade as currently implemented (the SUM-gate override, p_i/p_i_ref * basal_prob, over-drives the flagella TUs once basal_prob is properly calibrated). The mechanistic results (seam neutrality, Class II>III ordering, FlgM->FliA release, ordered NFsim assembly) are unaffected — only the count claim flips.

Question. Can a mechanistic transcriptional regulatory cascade — rather than manual multipliers / stoichiometry tweaks / overrides — give the E. coli whole-cell model temporally ordered flagellar gene expression and biologically feasible flagella counts? Concretely: does a Kalir & Alon (Cell 2004) bilinear SUM-gate driving promoter initiation, coupled to FlgM/sigma-28 sequestration relieved by type-III secretion through assembled flagella, reproduce the Class II -> Class III ordering (FlhDC/FliA genes first, then fliC/motAB/cheAW after hook-basal-body completion)?

Hypothesis. Maya Abdalla's prelim (Specific Aim 2): the WCM currently OVERPRODUCES flagella (~48 vs a biological handful) because the regulatory machinery is synthesized but never used to gate flagellar production. Embedding the Kalir & Alon SUM-gate as a FlagellaTranscriptionRegulation process — Class II weighted toward FlhD4C2, Class III toward free FliA — with FlgM holding FliA below threshold until basal-body completion (FlgMSecretion then releases it) will produce temporally ordered expression and feasible counts WITHOUT manual overrides. With the feature off the model is byte-neutral (init_prob_override stays 0; transcript_initiation unchanged).

🧬 Biology — the mechanism this investigation models E. coli builds its flagella "just in time" through a three-class transcriptional hierarchy. The master regulator FlhD4C2 (Class I) activates Class II genes (the…

E. coli builds its flagella "just in time" through a three-class transcriptional hierarchy. The master regulator FlhD4C2 (Class I) activates Class II genes (the hook-basal-body apparatus + fliA, the flagellar sigma factor sigma-28). FliA is held inactive by the anti-sigma factor FlgM. Only once a hook-basal body is complete does its type-III secretion system export FlgM, freeing FliA to fire the Class III genes (filament flagellin fliC, the motor motAB, chemotaxis cheAW). This delay is the molecular clock that orders assembly. Kalir & Alon (Cell 2004) quantified the FlhDC/FliA promoter weights as a bilinear SUM-gate; this investigation embeds that gate in the whole-cell model so flagellar expression is governed mechanistically rather than by hand-tuned overrides.

🔬 Scientific argument 5 for · 4 against Mechanistic transcriptional regulation — the Kalir & Alon SUM-gate coupled to FlgM/sigma-28 sequestration relieved by type-III secretion — gives the…

Main claim. Mechanistic transcriptional regulation — the Kalir & Alon SUM-gate coupled to FlgM/sigma-28 sequestration relieved by type-III secretion — gives the v2ecoli whole-cell model temporally ordered flagellar expression WITHOUT the manual multipliers/overrides the current WCM relies on. It does NOT lower flagella counts — under calibration it raises them (4-seed x 3-gen calibrated ensemble, ON > OFF in 11/12 seed-generations); the fast-mode reduction was an artifact. NFsim rule-based assembly additionally supplies the ordered, conditional construction that stochastic Gillespie complexation cannot.

Evidence for

  • The SUM-gate writes per-promoter init_prob_override with Class II > Class III, and the ordering is maintained across a cell division (study 02).
  • FlgM is secreted (1481 -> 5) and free FliA is released but stays bounded (~1.35x initial) via the flgM negative-feedback loop (study 03).
  • (Mechanistic, cache-independent) the cascade is wired and functional; the count direction is covered under evidence_against, not here.
  • NFsim assembles complete flagella through ordered intermediates (export -> motor -> hook -> flagellum); 9 complete flagella in 2400 s (study 04).
  • Under a low-flagella initial condition (study 03), the Class III override starts at exactly 0 and rises only as FlgM is secreted (1481 -> 115) — the assembly-gated Class II -> Class III onset, made explicit.

Evidence against

  • CALIBRATION REVERSAL (multi-seed confirmed) — on the full-mode calibrated cache the regulated lineage has MORE flagella, not fewer, robustly across a 4-seed x 3-gen ensemble (ON means 62.5/54.8/59.0 vs OFF means 49.5/44.2/40.8; ON > OFF in 11 of 12 seed-generations). The fast-mode reduction was an artifact; the cascade as implemented over-drives flagella expression.
  • The reduction within one generation is modest; the full overexpression -> biological-count correction is not demonstrated.
  • All lineages are single-seed, daughter-1-carry-forward; robustness across seeds/daughters is untested.
  • The assembly-gated Class III onset is shown only under a hand-set low-flagella initial condition (study 03); from the default already-flagellated cache the cascade shows the magnitude ordering but not the onset delay.

  • The transcriptional cascade (Aim 2A) and the NFsim assembly (Aim 2B) run as separate opt-in pieces; NFsim is standalone, not yet wired to replace ecoli-complexation inside the WCM.
  • Spatial organization (Aim 1) is out of scope.

Overview

This study asks whether (a) How over-expressed are flagellar components in the unregulated WCM baseline?. We recorded 2 findings confirm the expected biology, 1 contradict it. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. (a) How over-expressed are flagellar components in the unregulated WCM baseline? (b) Is the flagella_regulation port byte-neutral when the feature is off? ("Byte-neutral" = with the feature OFF, the model produces bit-for-bit identical output to pre-port main — adding the flagella code changes NOTHING you can observe until you switch it on. This is what lets us attribute every downstream difference to the cascade, not to the port.)
Mechanism / Model change. With features=[] the two flagella Steps are not wired and the promoter init_prob_override field stays 0.0 everywhere, so transcript_initiation's substitution (guarded on > 0) never fires — identical initiation probabilities to pre-port main. Flagellar component counts (CPLX0-7452, flagellin, motor) are read straight from the unregulated baseline for comparison against the regulated runs in flagella-02 / flagella-03.
Expected outcome. init_prob_override == 0 for every promoter across the run; cell grows/divides normally; flagellar component counts sit at the (over-expressed) unregulated level that the cascade is intended to bring down.

Overview

This study asks whether does Class II init_prob_override rise before Class III, with Class III gated. We recorded 2 findings confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Does Class II init_prob_override rise before Class III, with Class III gated until complete flagella (CPLX0-7452) accumulate and FlgM (G369-MONOMER) is secreted, releasing free FliA (EG11355-MONOMER / sigma-28)?
Mechanism / Model change. Promoter activity p_i = (beta*X + beta'*Y)/(beta+beta') with X=[FlhDC]/(K+[FlhDC]), Y=[free FliA]/(K+[FliA]). Class II beta-weighted (FlhDC), Class III beta'-weighted (FliA). The SUM-gate writes p_i (normalized to basal scale) to promoters.init_prob_override; transcript_initiation substitutes it where > 0.
Expected outcome. Mean Class III override trajectory lags mean Class II override; Class III stays near 0 while FliA is sequestered, rising as free FliA is released.

Biology

Type-III secretion depletes cytoplasmic FlgM in proportion to complete flagella, and the FlgM-FliA equilibrium releases free FliA — the anti-sigma-factor gate fires (MODEL mechanism).

Free FliA rises as FlgM is secreted but stays within a bounded band rather than running away — the flgM Class III negative-feedback loop caps it (BIOLOGY-level: the runaway sigma-28 seen without the loop is prevented).

From a low-flagella initial condition the Class III override starts near 0 and rises only as FlgM is secreted — the assembly-gated Class II -> Class III onset delay that the default already-flagellated cache hides.

Overview

This study asks whether does the FlgM secretion gate (exported ∝ complete flagella) deplete cytoplasmic. We recorded 2 findings confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Does the FlgM secretion gate (exported ∝ complete flagella) deplete cytoplasmic FlgM (G369-MONOMER[c]), shift the FlgM-FliA equilibrium to release free FliA (EG11355-MONOMER[c]), and keep FliA bounded via the flgM negative-feedback loop?
Mechanism / Model change. ecoli-flagella-flgm-secretion: exported = min(FlgM, round(n_flagella * 0.1 * dt)). FLGM-FLIA-CPLX equilibrium sequesters FliA; as FlgM falls, FliA is released. flgM is itself driven as a Class III gene (override = Y): as free FliA rises, flgM transcription rises, making more FlgM to re-sequester FliA — the cap that prevents the runaway FliA seen without this loop (Stefan et al. 2015, PLoS Comput Biol 11:e1004028).
Expected outcome. Cytoplasmic FlgM falls when flagella are present; free FliA rises then plateaus within a plausible band relative to its initial pool rather than growing without bound.

Biology

The pbg-nfsim NFSimProcess runs the flagella BNGL (237 rules, 7 sequential reactions) under BioNetGen and returns observable trajectories (MODEL runs).

Assembly intermediates appear in order (export apparatus -> motor -> hook) and complete flagella accumulate — the ordered, conditional construction that a plain Gillespie complexation cannot enforce (BIOLOGY-level: just-in-time hierarchy).

This is a STANDALONE assembly model — it is not yet coupled into the WCM, so it does not test whether SUM-gate-regulated monomer supply drives ordered assembly end to end. That coupling is the unstarted full Aim 2B.

Overview

This study asks whether does NFsim rule-based assembly reproduce ordered, hierarchical flagellar. We recorded 2 findings confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: In progress. Continue analysing run outcomes.

Purpose & background (study design)
Question. Does NFsim rule-based assembly reproduce ordered, hierarchical flagellar construction (basal body before hook before filament) that the stochastic Gillespie complexation cannot?
Mechanism / Model change. pbg_nfsim.NFSimProcess wraps BioNetGen/NFsim on flagella_complexation.bngl (237 rules, 7 sequential reactions). MonomerProduction feeds the ~30 free monomers; NFsim assembles them through the ordered reaction rules into the export apparatus, motor, hook, and finally the complete flagellum.
Expected outcome. Intermediates appear in assembly order and complete flagella accumulate, with free monomer pools incorporated into higher-order structures over time.

Conclusion synthesis

Read-only synthesis derived from the study's canonical fields (findings, limitations, follow-up proposals).

Claims
  • The pbg-nfsim NFSimProcess runs the flagella BNGL (237 rules, 7 sequential reactions) under BioNetGen and returns observable trajectories (MODEL runs).
  • Assembly intermediates appear in order (export apparatus -> motor -> hook) and complete flagella accumulate — the ordered, conditional construction that a plain Gillespie complexation cannot enforce (BIOLOGY-level: just-in-time hierarchy).
  • This is a STANDALONE assembly model — it is not yet coupled into the WCM, so it does not test whether SUM-gate-regulated monomer supply drives ordered assembly end to end. That coupling is the unstarted full Aim 2B.
Evidence
  • BioNetGen executes; observable trajectories returned over the 2400 s run
  • 2400 s: export=2, motor=1, hook=12, complete flagella=9, appearing in assembly order
  • monomers fed by a simple MonomerProduction step, not by WCM transcription
